boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Midtown destinations on corridors surrounding Touro University’s 3 Times Square campus, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Times Square Pedestrian Plazas — car-free pause
cards.subtitle: Broadway and Seventh Avenue, around West 42nd–47th Streets
cards.notes: Use the Broadway plazas as a walking route between campus and 47th Street; curb cuts make this public-space stretch more navigable.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrianized Midtown route with accessible curb cuts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Times Square Alliance identifies the Broadway plazas as wheelchair-friendly and says Times Square is open and accessible to all.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plazas; the Alliance notes peak pedestrian periods are typically noon–2 PM and 4–7 PM.

cards.title: TKTS Booth — same-day theater tickets
cards.subtitle: Broadway and Seventh Avenue at West 47th Street
cards.notes: Check the board for same-day Broadway and Off-Broadway availability, then decide whether the listed discount and show time fit your plan.
cards.short_summary: A staffed same-day ticket point beneath the Red Steps.
cards.evidence_claim: The Times Square Alliance states that the TKTS booth under the Red Steps offers same-day discounted tickets to dozens of Broadway and Off-Broadway shows.
cards.access_notes: The Alliance lists varying daily booth hours and notes that availability can change hourly.

cards.title: Bryant Park Lawn — outdoor programming
cards.subtitle: Bryant Park, between Fifth and Sixth Avenues at West 40th–42nd Streets
cards.notes: Check the park’s daily message before heading over; the lawn hosts activities and may close temporarily for weather or maintenance.
cards.short_summary: A central lawn used for seasonal events and everyday breaks.
cards.evidence_claim: Bryant Park says its lawn hosts large-scale events including Yoga and Movie Nights and can close for weather, aeration, fertilization, or protection.
cards.access_notes: Lawn availability is weather-dependent; consult the park homepage for the daily status.

cards.title: Bryant Park Reading Room — scheduled literary events
cards.subtitle: Bryant Park, Sixth Avenue corridor at West 40th–42nd Streets
cards.notes: Use the park calendar to find a Reading Room talk or workshop, and arrive with enough time to locate the programmed area.
cards.short_summary: A named Bryant Park venue with readings and workshops on its calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Bryant Park’s current calendar lists Reading Room author events and a fiction-writing workshop.
cards.access_notes: Programming changes by date; check the park calendar before going.

cards.title: Le Carrousel — a 14-animal ride
cards.subtitle: Bryant Park’s West 40th Street mid-block entrance
cards.notes: Find the carousel at the park’s south side and review its seasonal schedule before walking over; weather can affect operation.
cards.short_summary: A French-style carousel with 14 replica animals.
cards.evidence_claim: Bryant Park describes Le Carrousel as a 14-animal carousel and publishes seasonal hours and per-ride prices.
cards.access_notes: Hours are seasonal and weather permitting; rides require a ticket.

cards.title: NYPL Main Branch — research collections
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue at West 42nd Street
cards.notes: Enter from Fifth Avenue or the accessible 40th/42nd Street entrances, then use the Visitor Center to orient yourself to services.
cards.short_summary: NYPL’s flagship research building on the Fifth Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL identifies the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building at Fifth Avenue and 42nd Street as a premier research center with historical collections.
cards.access_notes: NYPL lists accessible entrances at 40th and 42nd Streets and asks visitors to check current building hours.

cards.entity_name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library Rooftop Terrace
cards.title: SNFL Rooftop Terrace — open-air seating
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue at East 40th Street
cards.notes: Enter the library at 455 Fifth Avenue and ask staff for the terrace route; pair the visit with browsing or a library-card errand.
cards.short_summary: A public rooftop terrace above NYPL’s largest circulating branch.
cards.evidence_claim: NYPL describes SNFL’s rooftop terrace as a free outdoor public space with Midtown views and open-air seating.
cards.access_notes: NYPL lists the library as fully accessible and publishes current branch hours on its location page.

cards.title: Grand Central Terminal — transit and architecture
cards.subtitle: East 42nd Street at Park Avenue
cards.notes: Walk east along 42nd Street to the main entrance and use the terminal’s official map to locate the concourse or transit connections.
cards.short_summary: A public terminal with rail, subway, bus, and architectural details.
cards.evidence_claim: Grand Central Terminal lists its main entrance at 89 East 42nd Street and identifies subway, bus, Metro-North, and LIRR connections.
cards.access_notes: The terminal is listed as open to the public daily; individual businesses and services have separate hours.

cards.title: Empire State Building — landmark exterior
cards.subtitle: West 34th Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues
cards.notes: Approach via West 34th Street and use the official directions page to choose a subway route before deciding whether to book an observatory visit.
cards.short_summary: An identifiable Art Deco landmark on the 34th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Empire State Building’s official visitor information places the building at 20 West 34th Street and provides walking and subway directions.
cards.access_notes: The official page provides directions; check the attraction’s current ticketing information separately if entering the observatory.

cards.title: Morgan Library & Museum — research-library setting
cards.subtitle: Madison Avenue at East 36th Street
cards.notes: Head east from the Fifth Avenue corridor to 225 Madison Avenue, then consult the museum’s visit information for exhibitions and admission details.
cards.short_summary: A museum and non-circulating research library on Madison Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Morgan states that it is located at 225 Madison Avenue at 36th Street and is a museum and non-circulating research library.
cards.source_title: The Morgan Library & Museum Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: The Morgan lists Free Friday Evenings with advance reservations; regular admission and exhibition details should be checked before visiting.
